targetTest: `cancel --wait` records the request, says so, and follows the run to cancelled
expected: With a supervisor whose unit hangs, cancel --wait prints 'cancel requested' then 'cancelled' within a few lease ticks: the lease timer reads the request and aborts the unit, the attempt ends cancelled and nothing is classified or retried; a request that lands as item A finishes cancels the run before B launches; a supervisor started on a run with a request standing cancels it at entry with no stage and no unit
actual: The supervisor ignored the request: the unit hung for its whole 40 s limit (the wait took 40536 ms), the run went on to ready_for_review in the between-items case and the entry case ran its stages and launched a unit instead of cancelling
semanticAssessment: The failures are assertion failures on elapsed time, final state, launched-unit count and checkpoint contents, never load or import errors: the fixtures start real supervisors with the fake run host, the helper composes main() on a fake terminal and the tracer tests of Task 1 in the same file pass. The wait path of the command finishes the cancel itself once the unit ends at its own limit, which is why the cancelled line and the attempt outcome already pass; only the timing and the no-retry facts do not.
